cls: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), propionic acid derivative
quick: 200-400 mg PO every 4-6 h (OTC); Rx up to 3200 mg/day
Take with food or milk to reduce GI upset
Avoid from 20 weeks; contraindicated from 30 weeks
Avoid in significant renal impairment; risk of AKI
Caution; avoid in severe hepatic impairment
BP, renal function, Hgb/GI symptoms on chronic use
summary: Ibuprofen is a widely used propionic-acid NSAID with analgesic, antipyretic and anti-inflammatory effects via non-selective COX inhibition. It carries the NSAID class BOXED WARNINGS for cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious GI bleeding/ulceration. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. Avoid in late pregnancy (>=30 weeks) and in significant renal disease.

dosage.n: OTC max 1200 mg/day without physician direction

dosage.d: 400-800 mg three to four times daily
dosage.n: Max 3200 mg/day; use lowest effective dose

admin: Take with food, milk or a full glass of water to reduce GI upset
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Do not combine with other NSAIDs or exceed the maximum daily dose
Stay hydrated; avoid in volume depletion
Patients on low-dose aspirin: take ibuprofen at least 8 h before or 30 min after aspirin to avoid blocking aspirin's antiplatelet effect
moa: Ibuprofen non-selectively and reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and -2 (COX-1/COX-2), reducing synthesis of prostaglandins that mediate inflammation, pain and fever. Antipyresis results from action on the hypothalamic heat-regulating center; analgesia and anti-inflammatory effects from reduced peripheral prostaglandin production.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria or allergic reaction after aspirin or other NSAIDs (aspirin triad)
Setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
Pregnancy at or after 30 weeks gestation
relative: Active or history of peptic ulcer/GI bleeding
Use from 20 weeks of pregnancy (risk of fetal renal dysfunction/oligohydramnios)
Concomitant anticoagulants, corticosteroids or other NSAIDs

preg: Avoid use at and after 20 weeks of gestation (risk of fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios); contraindicated at and after 30 weeks (premature closure of the ductus arteriosus). Limit use earlier in pregnancy to clear need.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding; only minimal amounts pass into milk. Generally considered a preferred NSAID during lactation.
renal: Can cause sodium/fluid retention, reduced GFR and acute kidney injury, especially with volume depletion, heart failure, or concomitant ACEi/ARB/diuretics. Avoid in significant renal impairment; not recommended in advanced renal disease.
hepatic: Can elevate transaminases and rarely cause serious hepatic reactions. Use with caution; avoid in severe hepatic impairment and monitor on chronic therapy.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) - markedly increased GI bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs / aspirin (anti-inflammatory doses) - additive GI and renal toxicity
Aspirin (low-dose cardioprotective) - ibuprofen can block its antiplatelet effect
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of AKI ('triple whammy')
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset (slightly delays absorption).
interactions.alcohol: Limit; increases risk of GI bleeding and ulceration.
interactions.diagnostics: May reduce measured creatinine clearance and cause sodium retention; can prolong bleeding time.

monitoring: Blood pressure, especially with chronic use
Renal function and electrolytes in at-risk patients
Hemoglobin/hematocrit and GI symptoms with prolonged use
counsel: Take with food or milk and the lowest effective dose for the shortest time
Stop and seek care for black/bloody stools, vomiting blood, or severe stomach pain
Report chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness or slurred speech (heart/stroke signs)
Avoid alcohol and other NSAIDs; tell your provider about all medicines
If you take low-dose aspirin for your heart, ask how to time ibuprofen so it does not block aspirin
pk: Analgesia within ~30 min; antipyresis within ~1 h
Store at 20-25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: NSAID class BOXED WARNINGS: cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious GI bleeding
Avoid from 20 weeks of pregnancy; contraindicated from 30 weeks
Can blunt the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin - separate dosing
'Triple whammy' (NSAID + ACEi/ARB + diuretic) markedly raises AKI risk
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
missed: For scheduled (anti-inflammatory) dosing, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up. For as-needed pain/fever use, simply take when needed.
overdose: Overdose can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness, and in large ingestions seizures, metabolic acidosis, renal failure and CNS/respiratory depression. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, activated charcoal if early, and monitor renal function, electrolytes and acid-base status. Dialysis is of limited value (high protein binding).
